Response of one variable to one shock at a fixed horizon, across all dates

Source: R/tvp.R
irf_path.Rd

Evolution over time of \(\Theta_{h}^{ij}(t)\), the response of variable \(i\) to recursive shock \(j\) at horizon \(h\) computed with frozen date-\(t\) parameters (see irf.tvpvar()). This is the usual "time-varying IRF" plot: for example the impact (or 8-quarter) response of inflation to a policy shock through time. With normalise_to the shock is rescaled each date so the impact response of variable equals size (e.g. 1 percentage point on the policy rate), removing changes in shock size.

Usage

irf_path(
  object,
  shock,
  response,
  horizon = 0L,
  normalise_to = NULL,
  size = 1,
  level = 0.68
)

Arguments

object

a tvpvar() fit.

shock, response

<tidy-select> one variable each.

horizon

horizon of the response (0 = impact).

normalise_to

optional <tidy-select> variable whose impact response is normalised to size.

size

normalised impact (default 1).

level

credible level of the band.

Value

a tvpvar_path tibble with columns date, estimate (posterior median), conf.low, conf.high; autoplot() plots it.

See also

Other TVP-VAR: tidy.tvpvar(), tvp_dynamics, tvp_prior(), tvp_volatility(), tvpvar()

Examples

# \donttest{
fit <- tvpvar(yraw, p = 2, ndraw = 200, nburn = 200)
irf_path(fit, shock = rate, response = infl, horizon = 4)
#> # A tibble: 173 × 4
